ai.description: *Ophisops pushkarensis* (Lacertidae) reaches 45 mm SVL. It is brownish-grey with two distinct dorsolateral white stripes and lacks movable eyelids. It features a single frontonasal scale.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ophisops pushkarensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a single, undivided supraocular scale, whereas most similar Indian *Ophisops* species possess two.
ai.habitat: *Ophisops pushkarensis* inhabits arid, sandy, or rocky scrublands in Rajasthan, typically found in open areas with sparse xerophytic vegetation at low altitudes.
ai.behavior: *Ophisops pushkarensis* is a diurnal lizard that actively forages for small insects by darting across open, sandy ground in arid scrublands.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ophisops pushkarensis* is oviparous, laying a clutch of 2–4 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from July to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ophisops pushkarensis* is endemic to the semi-arid regions of Rajasthan, India, specifically found in the Pushkar valley at elevations around 500 meters.
